# What Should Be Checked First in the Original Thread When Action and qpos Are Not Consistent in Isaac Lab?

> **Current answer:** Isaac Lab contributors recommend first troubleshooting by calibrating the robot simulation and verifying the used actuator models. Once the model is deemed reliable, domain randomization can be used to expand the training distribution, improving robustness to joint position errors. This is only a diagnostic step and not a verified fix.

## Problem and symptoms

- The absolute joint angle action is not fully followed by qpos in Isaac Lab, while the real robot can follow it.
- Simulation qpos does not match the action; single-step action variation can exceed 1 rad; real robot can follow after interpolation.

## Environment

- Custom ALOHA URDF to USD; custom switch furniture environment; implicit actuator; angular units are in rad.

## Priority diagnostics

- The contributors recommend first confirming the robot tuning status and actuator model, and then considering noise and domain randomization.
